He played college basketball for the Duke Blue Devils alongside Zion Williamson and Cam Reddish. Born in [[Toronto]] as the son of former basketball player [[Rowan Barrett]], Barrett shone at [[St. Marcellinus Secondary School]] in [[Mississauga]], Ontario before transferring to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]]. He was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the consensus top recruit in the 2018 class, earning [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] and [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] accolades in his final high school season. He was ranked the top player in his class by all recruiting services and was the first player since LeBron James to sweep all major awards in high school and win the national championship. Barrett is expected to be a top 3 pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]]. With the [[Canada national under-19 basketball team|Canadian national under-19 team]], Barrett was named [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|MVP]] at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] after leading his team to a gold medal. He debuted for the senior team during [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)|qualification]] for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]]. ==Early life and career== Barrett was born in [[Toronto]], Ontario to Kesha Duhaney and [[Rowan Barrett]]. Early in his childhood, he developed an interest in basketball and played with a mini-hoop in his playroom in France, where his father was playing professional basketball.{{cite web |last1=Grange |first1=Michael |title=Poster Boy: Rowan Barrett Jr. Rising |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/poster-boy-rowan-barrett-jr-rising/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |accessdate=January 5, 2019 |date=August 17, 2015}} While living in France, Barrett attended a French school but was taught English by his mother.{{cite web |last1=Davis |first1=Seth |title=Canada rising: R.J. Barrett’s college announcement will move him one step closer to conquering the world |url=https://theathletic.com/149076/2017/11/08/canada-rising-r-j-barretts-college-announcement-will-move-him-one-step-closer-to-conquering-the-world/ |publisher=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=January 7, 2019 |date=November 8, 2017}} He lived in a number of countries due to his father's career and [[Shootaround|shot around]] after games and practices. Barrett additionally played basketball with players his age through the clubs his father was a part of.{{cite web |last1=Salvian |first1=Haley |title=Like father, like son: R.J. and Rowan Barrett |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/rj-rowan-barrett-father-son-dynamic-1.4649826 |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |accessdate=January 6, 2019 |date=May 6, 2018}} His family settled in [[Mississauga]], Ontario in 2008, when his father left professional basketball. While growing up, he was also involved in [[association football|football]], [[100 metres]] sprinting, and the [[high jump]].{{cite web |last1=Ewing |first1=Lori |title=Canadian basketball star R.J. Barrett to jump a year ahead to join Class of 2018 |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/canadian-basketball-star-rj-barrett-to-jump-a-year-ahead-to-join-class-of-2018/article35843179/ |website=[[The Globe and Mail]] |accessdate=January 5, 2019 |date=July 31, 2017}} At age 12, after struggling in a basketball game and coming home crying, Barrett began focusing on basketball instead of football to avoid missing tournaments. At that age, he told his father that he wanted to be an [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and make the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Basketball Hall of Fame]]. He sometimes trained with [[Steve Nash]], his [[godparent|godfather]] and father's friend.{{cite web |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=RJ Barrett inherited a Canada that Vince Carter built |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25707107/how-vince-carter-paved-way-rj-barrett |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=January 8, 2019}} Barrett, under the guidance of his father, emerged as one of the best under-12 players in Ontario. He attended Horizon Jeunesse in [[Clarkson, Mississauga]], leading his school team to a city title for Mississauga French elementary schools, where he was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) despite facing older opponents. Barrett also played for the Regional Elite Development Academy (REDA) under-12 program on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit, facing many teams from the United States.{{cite web |last1=Colpitts |first1=Iain |title=Like father, like son |url=https://www.mississauga.com/community-story/3119703-like-father-like-son/ |website=[[The Mississauga News]] |accessdate=January 5, 2019 |date=August 29, 2011}} When he was 12, he was identified by the Ontario Basketball Association as one of the best players in his age group, and he consequently trained with the [[Canada Basketball]] junior academy, through which he competed for the Ontario provincial team. By age 15, Barrett was generally playing the [[point guard]] position. On August 3, 2014, he scored 37 points and grabbed 7 rebounds in a 93–53 win over Quebec at an under-15 provincial tournament.{{cite web |last1=Sbiet |first1=Tariq |title=Team Ontario 15s Prove Dominance, Rowan Barrett Jr Explodes for 37 |url=http://northpolehoops.com/2014/08/03/team-ontario-15s-prove-dominance-rowan-barrett-jr-explodes-for-37/ |publisher=North Pole Hoops |accessdate=January 5, 2019 |date=August 3, 2014}} Through Grades 7 and 8, Barrett attended École Secondaire Jeunes Sans Frontières, a French language school in [[Brampton]].{{cite web |last1=Vallière |first1=Kim |title=R.J. Barrett, possible premier choix de la NBa et francophone |url=http://www.sympatico.ca/actualites/nouvelles/regions/ottawa-gatineau/r-j-barrett-possible-premier-choix-de-la-nba-et-francophone-1.3978124 |accessdate=January 6, 2019 |language=French |date=July 2, 2018}} ==High school career== ===St. Marcellinus (2014–15)=== {{quote box |quote="While we don't often give praise in the early stages of a player's career (ninth grade), Rowan Barrett Jr (2019 6'4 wing) is proving to be the exception—a cold blooded killer, still out for blood. Special." |source= — Elias Sbiet, analyst for recruiting website North Pole Hoops, on Barrett in 2014. |width=25em |align=right}} Barrett began high school at [[St. Marcellinus Secondary School]] in Mississauga, while competing for the Brampton Warriors AAU team through the REDA.{{cite web |last1=Acquisto |first1=Stella |title=Canada's next great hoops star has championship pedigree |url=https://toronto.citynews.ca/2015/09/21/canadas-next-great-hoops-star-comes-has-championship-pedigree/ |publisher=[[CityNews]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=September 21, 2015}} After his 27-point effort for St. Marcellinus against [[Bill Crothers Secondary School]] on October 9, 2014, Canadian recruiting website North Pole Hoops labeled him "special" despite only being in his first year.{{cite web |last1=Sbiet |first1=Elias |title=Rowan Barrett Jr Proving To Be Special |url=http://northpolehoops.com/2014/10/09/rowan-barrett-jr-proving-to-be-special/ |publisher=North Pole Hoops |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=October 9, 2014}} In February 2015, he was named MVP of the Guy Vetrie Memorial tournament after scoring 41 points and a making the game-winner for REDA in a 74–72 win over BTB Academy.{{cite web |last1=Coccimiglio |first1=Brad |title=Senior final goes down to the wire at Guy Vetrie Memorial |url=https://www.sootoday.com/local-sports/senior-final-goes-down-to-the-wire-at-guy-vetrie-memorial-5-photos-178602 |website=[[Village Media|Soo Today]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=February 8, 2015}} In April, Barrett was invited to the [[Region of Peel Secondary Schools Athletic Association]] (ROPSSAA) all-star game.{{cite web |last1=Colpitts |first1=Iain |title=Local players selected for Peel All-Star Game |url=https://www.mississauga.com/community-story/5538073-local-players-selected-for-peel-all-star-game/ |website=[[The Mississauga News]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=April 2, 2015}} At the game, he was recognized as the best prospect in the ROPSSAA.{{cite web |last1=Juzenas |first1=Frank |title=Buzzer-beater wins all-star game |url=https://www.bramptonguardian.com/community-story/5562153-buzzer-beater-wins-all-star-game/ |website=[[Brampton Guardian]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019}} In the same month, Barrett scored a game-high 25 points in the Futures Game at the [[BioSteel All-Canadian Basketball Game]], which featured top Grade 9 and 10 players across Canada.{{cite web |title=Murray, Poyser MVPs of BioSteel All-Canadian game |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/murray-poyser-mvps-of-biosteel-all-canadian-game/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=April 14, 2015}}{{cite web |last1=Colpitts |first1=Iain |title=Poyser, Barrett shine in Biosteel All Canadian showcase |url=https://www.mississauga.com/community-story/5559887-poyser-barrett-shine-in-biosteel-all-canadian-showcase/ |website=[[The Mississauga News]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=April 15, 2015}} ===Montverde Academy (2015–18)=== ====Freshman year (2015–16)==== In September 2015, one week after touring top [[College-preparatory school|prep schools]] in the United States, Barrett announced that he would leave St. Marcellinus.{{cite web |last1=Ebanks |first1=Drew |title=St. Marcellinus Spirit not joining newly formed OSBA |url=https://onpointbasketball.com/st-marcellinus-spirit-not-joining-newly-formed-osba/ |publisher=On Point Basketball |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=September 21, 2015}} Later in the month, he transferred to [[Montverde Academy]], a school in [[Montverde, Florida]] with a decorated basketball program.{{cite web |last1=Okrainetz |first1=Chris |title=Canada’s Top Prospect Rowan Barrett Jr. Heading to Montverde Academy |url=https://tipofthetower.com/2015/09/23/canadas-top-prospect-rowan-barrett-jr-heading-to-montverde-academy/ |publisher=Tip of the Tower |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=September 23, 2015}} Barrett made the decision in order to "take his game to another level" but described the transition as "rough."{{cite web |last1=Gardenour |first1=Jeff |title=Soph sensation R.J. Barrett leads Montverde |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-hs-sp-rj-barrett-montverde-0126-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=January 25, 2017}} On December 7, he chipped in a team-high 18 points in a nationally televised game versus [[Huntington Prep School]].{{cite web |last1=DelGallo |first1=Alicia |title=Montverde shows off with win for ESPN |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-hs-huntington-montverde-boys-basketball-1208y-content-1208-20151207-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=December 7, 2015}} Barrett erupted for 31 points on December 21, in a loss to [[Chino Hills High School]] at the City of Palms Classic quarterfinal.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=No. 2 Chino Hills edges No. 1 Montverde in City of Palms quarterfinal |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/no-2-chino-hills-edges-no-1-montverde-in-city-of-palms-quarterfinal |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=December 21, 2015}} On April 15, 2016, he tallied 22 points and 8 rebounds at the 2016 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game, earning game MVP honors.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=Nigerian Charles Bassey makes up for late start, lifts Black team in International game at Jordan Classic |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/charles-bassey-r-j-barrett-montverde-academy-st-anthony-jordan-brand-classic |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=April 15, 2016}} At the end of the season, after leading Montverde Academy in scoring, Barrett was named to the [[MaxPreps]] Freshman All-American First Team.{{cite web |last1=Hickman |first1=Jason |title=2015-16 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Freshman All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/VBO3zMrQQUSqQAWAQvODAA/2015-16-maxpreps-boys-basketball-freshman-all-american-team.htm |website=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=April 21, 2016}} ====Sophomore year (2016–17)==== {{quote box |quote= "I love the kid. I think he's really, really talented. He can handle the ball, can get to the basketball at will; he's tough, he's competitive ... he can go both ways, offensively. Defensively he's not afraid to guard the best player on the other team. As a coach you can't ask for much more, which is why he's the camp MVP." |source= — [[Fred Vinson (basketball)|Fred Vinson]] on Barrett after coaching him at [[Basketball Without Borders]] in 2017 |width=25em |align=right}} Entering 2016–17, Barrett's sophomore season for Montverde, he was among 20 players named to the ''[[USA Today]]'' High School Sports All-USA Preseason Team.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=2016-17 American Family Insurance ALL-USA Preseason Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/2016-17-american-family-insurance-all-usa-preseason-boys-basketball-team#slideIdslide-2 |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=October 20, 2016}} In November 2016, he was named to the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award]] watch list.{{cite web |title=Naismith Trophy High School Boys All-America team announced |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/naismith-trophy-high-school-boys-all-america-team-announced |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=March 8, 2017}} In December, Barrett led Montverde to a City of Palms Classic title, scoring a team-best 15 points in the finals against [[East High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Memphis East High School]], and received tournament MVP honors.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=No. 4 Montverde Academy wins its third City of Palms title |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/no-4-montverde-academy-wins-its-third-city-of-palms-title |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=December 21, 2016}} He recorded 21 points on January 16, 2017, in a 73–67 win over [[Bishop Montgomery High School]], to help his team win the Spalding Hoophall Classic.{{cite web |title=Montverde Academy holds off Bishop Montgomery for win at Spalding Hoophall Classic |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/vU_p0VW18keCNGRcLBMCIA/montverde-academy-holds-off-bishop-montgomery-for-win-at-spalding-hoophall-classic.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=January 16, 2017}} In February, Barrett garnered MVP accolades at [[Basketball Without Borders]], a three-day camp during [[NBA All-Star Weekend]].{{cite web |last1=Grange |first1=Michael |title=Rowan Barrett Jr. among several Canadians with all-star potential |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/rowan-barrett-jr-among-several-canadians-star-potential/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=February 19, 2017}} He joined the World Select Team at the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in April, posting 9 points and 2 steals in 20 minutes.{{cite web |title=Nike Hoop Summit Box Scores |url=https://www.usab.com/mens/nike-hoop-summit/stats.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=January 10, 2019}}{{cite web |title=World Select Team Announced For 2017 Nike Hoop Summit |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2017/03/world-team-announced.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=March 15, 2017}} Barrett finished the season averaging 22 points and 7 rebounds per game in high school, being tabbed National Sophomore of the Year by MaxPreps and making the Naismith All-American Third Team.{{cite web |title=2016-17 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/MsrjHfTvwUaObsbpYQ-lYg/2016-17-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=April 13, 2017}}{{cite web |title=Naismith High School Boys’ All-American Team Announced |url=http://naismithtrophy.com/naismith-high-school-boys-all-american-team-announced/ |publisher=[[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith Trophy]] |accessdate=January 10, 2019 |date=March 8, 2017}} ====Junior year (2017–18)==== [[File:RJ Barrett (cropped) 2.jpg|thumb|Barrett at the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]]] On July 31, 2017, Barrett reclassified to the 2018 class because he believed he was "ready to move up and to be in college a year earlier."{{cite web |last1=Weinstein |first1=Josh |title='I'm right on track': Canada's R.J. Barrett reclassifies for 2019 NBA draft |url=https://torontosun.com/2017/07/31/im-right-on-track-canadas-rj-barrett-reclassifies-for-2019-nba-draft/wcm/30cf54c8-6fba-4379-8a79-7ead70f9ecdb |website=[[Toronto Sun]] |accessdate=January 12, 2019 |date=July 31, 2017}} Entering the 2017–18 season, he was named to the ''USA Today'' High School Sports All-USA Preseason Team.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=2017-18 American Family Insurance ALL-USA Preseason Boys Basketball Team |url=https://uasatodayhss.com/2017/2017-18-american-family-insurance-all-usa-preseason-boys-basketball-team |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 13, 2019 |date=November 27, 2017}} In his season opener on November 28, 2017, Barrett led Montverde, ranked the No. 1 team in the nation by MaxPreps, with 29 points in a 97–55 win over The Rock School.{{cite web |last1=Stover |first1=Tyler |title=Montverde pounds The Rock |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-montverde-basketball-1129-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |accessdate=January 13, 2019 |date=November 28, 2017}} On January 11, 2018, in a nationally televised match-up with [[Orlando Christian Prep]], he scored 24 points.{{cite web |last1=Fay |first1=Max |title=R.J. Barrett and Nassir Little show off on big stage |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-montverde-ocp-basketball-1112-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |accessdate=January 13, 2019 |date=January 11, 2018}} Barrett posted 22 points and 10 rebounds on January 15 to defeat [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]] at the Spalding Hoophall Classic.{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=No. 1 Montverde Academy coasts past Mater Dei |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/no-1-montverde-academy-coasts-past-mater-dei-hoophall-classic-rj-barrett |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=January 13, 2019 |date=January 15, 2018}} On March 23, he played in the Signature All-Canadian Showcase, which featured 24 top Canadian prospects.{{cite web |title=RJ Barrett Headlines Inaugural Signature All Canadian Showcase, NBA Certified Event |url=http://northpolehoops.com/2018/03/23/mississauga-hosts-inaugural-signature-canadian-showcase/ |publisher=North Pole Hoops |accessdate=January 13, 2019 |date=March 23, 2018}} Later in the month, Barrett took part in the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], where he scored 26 points.{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=McDonald's Recap: Nassir Little, R.J. Barrett steal the show |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/McDonalds-Recap-Nassir-Little-RJ-Barrett-steal-the-show--116802320/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=January 13, 2019 |date=March 28, 2018}} In March 2018, Barrett was awarded the prestigious [[Morgan Wootten National Player of the Year|Morgan Wooten National Player of the Year]] award for "displaying outstanding character, showing leadership and embodying the values of a student athlete."{{Cite news|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/mcdonald-american-games-announces-2018-130000092.html|title=McDonald’s All American Games Announces The 2018 Morgan Wootten Player Of The Year Award Winners|access-date=April 4, 2018|language=en-US}} One of the ways Barrett exhibited these attributes was by being involved in the Basketball Buddies Program of [[Montverde Academy]], where he was in charge of mentoring young basketball athletes with their basketball skills, as well as advising them on how to manage their academics.{{Cite news|url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/rj-barrett-named-2018-morgan-wootten-player-year/|title=RJ Barrett Named 2018 Morgan Wootten Player Of The Year|date=March 13, 2018|work=SLAMonline|accessdate=April 4, 2018}} In the 2017-18 season, he led the undefeated Montverde team to the Geico National boys’ basketball championship, recording 25 points and 15 rebounds in the championship game.{{Cite news|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/faVAispzyU-y2nf0VRAwbA/rj-barrett,-montverde-academy-add-cherry-on-top-with-geico-nationals-crown.htm|title=R.J. Barrett, Montverde Academy add 'cherry on top' with GEICO Nationals crown - MaxPreps|date=March 31, 2018|work=MaxPreps.com|access-date=April 19, 2018|language=en-US}} Barrett scored a game-high 20 points to go along with nine rebounds, six assists and five steals at the 2018 Nike Hoop Summit and was named MVP.{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketball.ca/ltad-s15158/news-article/world-select-team-defeats-usa-89-76-at-2018-nike-hoop-summit|title=Canada Basketball|website=www.basketball.ca|access-date=April 18, 2018}} ===Recruiting=== While attending St. Marcellinus Secondary School, Barrett was tabbed as the top Canadian prospect in the 2019 class.{{cite web |last1=Hickman |first1=Jason |title=MaxPreps 2015-16 High School Basketball Early Contenders |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/xNnLTtfQPEmCmcV8KyyTmQ/maxpreps-2015-16-high-school-basketball-early-contenders,-presented-by-dicks-sporting-goods-and-under-armour--montverde-academy.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=January 9, 2019 |date=November 10, 2015}} He received scholarship offers from several major universities including [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], according to ESPN. Speaking to nbadraft.net in April 2017, [[Roy Rana]], who coached Barrett at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] and at the Nike Hoop Summit, was quoted as saying about Barrett: "A star. A potential superstar down the road."{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2017-nike-hoop-summit-world-team-recap|title=2017 Nike Hoop Summit: World Team Recap {{!}} NBADraft.net|website=www.nbadraft.net|language=en|access-date=July 12, 2017}} On August 16, 2017, Barrett narrowed down to five schools: [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/8/16/16159478/rj-barrett-recruiting-duke-kentucky-arizona-michigan-oregon|title=New No. 1 recruit R.J. Barrett announces list of 5 finalists|work=SBNation.com|access-date=August 17, 2017}} On November 10, 2017, he announced that he would be attending Duke for the 2018-2019 season.{{Cite news|url=https://www.tsn.ca/canada-s-top-ranked-prospect-barrett-chooses-duke-1.912267|title=Canada’s top-ranked prospect Barrett chooses Duke - Article - TSN|date=November 10, 2017|work=TSN|access-date=November 11, 2017}} Commenting on his decision, he said: "It feels like home. And obviously they have a great coach ... I love [[Mike Krzyzewski|Coach K]]. I've been watching Duke since I was really young."{{Cite news|url=https://www.dukebasketballreport.com/2017/11/11/16636604/duke-recruiting-rj-barrett-will-be-a-blue-devil-basketball|title=Duke Recruiting RJ Barrett Will Be A Blue Devil|work=Duke Basketball Report|access-date=November 11, 2017}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = R. J. Barrett | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Mississauga|Mississauga, Ontario]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 200 | 40 = | commitdate = November 10, 2017 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Duke 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Duke Blue Devils Recruiting Class | rivals school = duke | 247 school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = 150 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 1 | 247 overall = 1 | espn overall = 1 | accessdate = June 30, 2018 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:RJ Barrett & Zion Williamson - Keenan Hairston (cropped) 2.jpg|thumb|Barrett (left) celebrates with [[Zion Williamson]] in December 2018]] Barrett made his preseason debut for Duke on August 15, 2018 in an 86–67 win over the Canadian [[Ryerson University]] [[Ryerson Rams|Rams]], scoring 34 points and collecting 5 rebounds while shooting 11-of-29 from the field.{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Duke's Zion Williamson, R.J. Barrett lead Blue Devils to exhibition rout of Ryerson |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/dukes-zion-williamson-r-j-barrett-lead-blue-devils-to-exhibition-rout-of-ryerson/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |accessdate=August 19, 2018 |date=August 16, 2018}} On November 6, in his first regular season game, he posted 33 points and 6 assists against No. 2-ranked [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] at the [[Champions Classic]], breaking the Duke freshman scoring record in a debut.{{cite web |title=Canada's R.J. Barrett breaks Duke record in sizzling college debut |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/rj-barrett-duke-record-1.4895210 |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |accessdate=January 12, 2019 |date=November 7, 2018}} Barrett tallied his first [[double (basketball)|double-double]] on December 5, with 27 points and 15 rebounds versus [[Hartford Hawks men's basketball|Hartford]].{{cite web |last1=McCreary |first1=Joedy |title=RJ Barrett leads No. 3 Duke past Hartford, 84-54 |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/college/hc-sp-hartford-duke-20181206-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=January 12, 2019 |date=December 6, 2018}} He had another strong performance in his next game against [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]], where he recorded 30 points, 7 rebounds, and 6 assists.{{cite web |last1=Lindqwister |first1=Winston |title=R.J. Barrett, stellar defense drive offense as Duke men's basketball takes down Yale |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2018/12/r-j-barrett-stellar-defense-drive-offense-as-duke-mens-basketball-takes-down-yale |website=[[The Chronicle (Duke University)|The Chronicle]] |accessdate=January 12, 2019 |date=December 8, 2018}} Barrett eclipsed the 30-point mark again on January 12, 2019, scoring 32 points in an 80–78 win over [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Tim |title=RJ Barrett, Duke Beat FSU on Cam Reddish Winner; Zion Williamson Drops 11 |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2815332-rj-barrett-duke-beat-fsu-on-cam-reddish-winner-zion-williamson-drops-11 |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=January 12, 2019 |date=January 12, 2019}} On February 17, Barrett recorded 23 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 94–78 win over [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]].http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26014002/rj-barrett-triple-double-propels-no-2-duke-nc-state It was the fourth time in Duke history (second time under [[Mike Krzyzewski]]'s tenure as head coach) where a player recorded a triple-double for the team.https://247sports.com/Article/RJ-Barrett-Duke-Blue-Devils-basketball-triple-double-129210254/https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/rj-barrett-records-the-4th-triple-double-in-dukes-history-news.72206.html At the end of Duke's regular season, Barrett was named a member of both the Sporting News' All-American First Team and the All-ACC First Team alongside his teammate [[Zion Williamson]]. On March 22, Barrett led the team in both points and rebounds with 26 points and 14 rebounds in an 85–62 win over no. 16 [[North Dakota State Bison men's basketball|North Dakota State]] in the NCAA Tournament.http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=211796767 He saw action in a total of 38 games (38 starts) as a freshman, averaging 22.6 points, 7.6 rebounds and 4.3 assists a contest.{{Cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=210461052&DB_OEM_ID=4200|title=Stats (PDF): Duke Combined Team Statistics (as of Mar 31, 2019)|last=|first=|date=|website=goduke.com|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=|access-date=2019-04-22}} Following Duke's loss in the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Barrett announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]], where he is projected to be a top three pick.{{Cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/dukes-rj-barrett-enters-2019-nba-draft-161121245.html|title=Duke F RJ Barrett enters 2019 NBA draft|work=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=April 10, 2019}} ==National team career== Barrett was the youngest player on Canada's under-16 national team that won silver at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|2015 FIBA Americas U16 Championship]], in [[Argentina]]. Pouring in 14.6 points a contest, he led his team in scoring during the tournament.{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaamericas.com/en/torneos_roster.asp?t=IECLYPFCDT&team=257&n=Canada&c=CAN|title=FIBA AMERICAS|website=www.fibaamericas.com|access-date=July 9, 2017}} He averaged 18.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2016 FIBA U17 World Cup]], in [[Spain]], en route to [[eurobasket.com]]'s All-World Cup U17 Second Team honours.{{Cite news|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/121265/sid/12180/tid/257/_/2016_FIBA_U17_World_Championship/index.html|title=Rowan Barrett profile, FIBA U17 World Championship 2016 {{!}} FIBA.COM|work=FIBA.COM|access-date=July 9, 2017}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/World-Championships-U17/basketball_2016_Men.asp|title=World Championships U17 Basketball, Teams, Scores, Stats, News, Standings - eurobasket|work=www.eurobasket.com|access-date=July 9, 2017}} In July 2017, Barrett made headlines with a 38-point, 13-rebound, and 5-assist showing as he guided Canada's under-19 squad to a 99–87 semifinal win over the US at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/world/u19/2017/news/canada-slay-usa-dragon-to-reach-historic-final|title=Canada slay USA dragon to reach historic Final|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=July 9, 2017}} At the time, Northpolehoops.com described this performance as Barrett's "biggest game of his career so far".{{Cite web|url=http://northpolehoops.com/2017/07/08/r-j-barrett-shakes-the-world-in-canadas-historic-win-over-usa/|title=R.J. Barrett shakes the world in Canada's historic win over USA|date=July 8, 2017|website=Northpolehoops.com|access-date=July 9, 2017}} He subsequently led Canada to the title, tallying game-highs of 18 points and 12 rebounds in the championship game against Italy, and was named to [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup All-Tournament Team|the tournament's All-Star Five]] and also [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|the tournament Most Valuable Player]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/canada-routs-italy-capture-gold-fiba-u19-basketball-world-cup/|title=Canada routs Italy to capture gold at FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup - Sportsnet.ca|work=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=July 9, 2017|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/world/u19/2017/news/barrett-named-mvp-after-winning-canada-s-first-u19-title|title=Barrett named MVP after winning Canada's first U19 title|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=July 10, 2017}} Averaging 21.6 points a game, he was also the leading scorer of the tournament.{{Cite web|url=https://fiba.com/world/u19/2017/playerstats|title=Players statistics of the FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2017 - FIBA.basketball|website=FIBA.basketball|language=en|access-date=July 12, 2017}} In June 2018, he made his debut on Canada's senior men's national team, scoring 16 points in a 97-62 win over China.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/rj-barrett-canada-basketball-victory-national-team-debut-1.4719457|title=R.J. Barrett leads Canada to victory in national team debut {{!}} CBC Sports|last=June 23|first=Jim Morris · The Canadian Press ·|website=CBC|language=en|access-date=December 8, 2018}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] | 38 || 38 || 35.3 || .454 || .308 || .665 || 7.6 || 4.3 || .9 || .4 || 22.6 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Barrett's father [[Rowan Barrett]] was born to Jamaican parents and raised in Toronto. He played college basketball for [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] before embarking on a professional career spent in Europe and South America.{{cite web |title=Former SJU Star Rowan Barrett Leading Team Canada |url=https://redstormsports.com/news/2000/9/19/Former_SJU_Star_Rowan_Barrett_Leading_Team_Canada.aspx?path=mbball |publisher=St. John's University Athletics |accessdate=January 6, 2019 |date=September 19, 2000}}{{cite web |title=Catch you on the rebound: Rowan Barrett |url=http://basketball.ca/staff-s15166/news-article/catch-you-on-the-rebound-rowan-barrett |publisher=[[Canada Basketball]] |accessdate=January 6, 2019}} Rowan Sr. was a long-time member of the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]], which he [[Captain (sports)|captained]] at the [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000 Summer Olympics]], and later became executive vice president and assistant general manager for Canada Basketball.{{cite web |last1=Gay |first1=Carlan |title=Executive VP Rowan Barrett praises players' commitment after qualifying for FIBA Basketball World Cup 2019 |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/rowan-barrett-praises-players-of-team-canada-basketball-usports-fiba-basketball-world-cup-2019/10gcvocgnmurc1v6vngcekakrk |publisher=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]] |accessdate=January 6, 2019 |date=December 6, 2018}} Barrett is the [[godparent|godson]] of [[Steve Nash]], a Basketball Hall of Fame inductee who played with his father on the Canadian national team.{{cite web |title=Point guards Steve Nash, Jason Kidd and Maurice Cheeks among Hall inductees |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24611047/steve-nash-jason-kidd-maurice-cheeks-basketball-hall-fame-inductees |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=January 7, 2019 |date=September 8, 2018}} Rowan Sr. first met Nash, who is about two years his junior, while playing for the [[Canada national under-19 basketball team|under-19 national team]] and quickly became close friends with him. When Barrett was a baby, Nash bought him his first [[infant bed|crib]]. Barrett's mother Kesha Duhaney is a native of [[Brooklyn]], New York. She was a nationally ranked [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]] and [[long jump]]er for [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's University]] before working for the [[Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce]].{{cite web |last1=Pecar |first1=Steve |title=Mississauga’s Barrett receives top basketball honour |url=https://peelregionreview.com/mississaugas-barrett-receives-top-basketball-honour/ |website=Peel Region Review |accessdate=January 6, 2019 |date=March 9, 2018}} Barrett's parents first met while attending St. John's. His maternal aunt [[Dahlia Duhaney]] was a member of the Jamaican [[4 × 100 metres relay|4 × 100 m relay]] team that won a gold medal at the [[1991 World Championships in Athletics|1991 IAAF World Championships]].{{cite web |title=Five things to know about rising Canadian basketball star R.J. Barrett |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/five-things-know-rising-canadian-basketball-star-r-j-barrett/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |accessdate=January 6, 2019 |date=November 10, 2017}} Also on his mother's side, his grandparents ran [[track and field|track]] for the Jamaican national team, and his uncle played [[American football|football]] for the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]. Barrett can speak French fluently, although he admitted to being "a little rusty" in 2018.{{cite web |last1=Ewing |first1=Lori |title=R.J. Barrett to make Duke debut in hometown of Toronto |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/rj-barrett-duke-canada-tour-1.4780868 |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]] |accessdate=January 8, 2018 |date=August 10, 2018}} He has a brother Nathan, who is about four years younger than him.
